idiom_name: sealed trait + case classes with exhaustive match; Pekko Event / EventSourcedBehavior
implementation_notes: sealed trait OrderEvent with final case class cases is the event contract: cases are immutable, equality is structural, and match on the trait is exhaustiveness-checked by the compiler, so the classic event class hierarchy and its type switch collapse into one idiomatic construct. Serialisation of the sealed hierarchy uses a JSON library's derivation (circe, jsoniter, play-json) with an explicit discriminator field, and delivery is Pekko's EventStream (publish/subscribe for local actors) or a broker client. When the events are also the system of record, Pekko's EventSourcedBehavior persists the same case classes - persist(event) inside onCommand - so the event message doubles as the event-sourcing entry, which is the strongest form of the pattern.
pitfalls: A sealed hierarchy must live in one file, so cross-module extension is deliberately impossible; splitting the trait and its cases breaks compilation - which is the point, but it must be planned for.
Deriving JSON for sealed traits without an explicit discriminator yields a wrapper/hint that other consumers cannot read; pin the discriminator in one place (codec configuration).
Pekko's EventStream is local to an ActorSystem and unordered across publishers; use a broker when the contract is cross-system.

Case classes holding mutable collections are only shallowly immutable, and structural equality means two identical events compare equal - do not use equality as an idempotency key unless duplicates really share an id.
